body:
subject: STORY-1350 requeued; #1970 merged; BUG-1291's fork decided — your instinct plus a backstop, and NOT the lock

Three things done, one fork decided.

STORY-1350 REQUEUED. The brief carries your two confirmed findings, your shared-constant point for the '## Implementer approach' marker (a marker that drifts breaks the loop with no test failing anywhere is a good catch), and an explicit restatement that criteria 4 and 5 stay out of scope so nobody implements the preview or the measurement I removed.

Your refusal to use AIDA_SESSION_ROLE=advisor was the right call, and the reason is now acceptance on STORY-1353 rather than sitting in a mailbox. The sharp form: the workaround is worse than the refusal, because it makes the audit trail say the ADVISOR queued it. A seat that must impersonate another seat to do its own job manufactures false provenance — and that record is exactly what EPIC-69's ledger would read. A correctly-behaved seat being left with no way to do its own job is the evidence that the gate is mis-drawn. I added that the test must assert the recorded ACTOR, not merely a zero exit.

#1970 MERGED at 14:22, BUG-1268 Completed. I reviewed the diff myself rather than merging on CI alone, and recorded the gap plainly: no reviewer has ever looked at that PR — zero reviewer-phase events for the spec — so the ledger says independence was PARTIAL, with codex authoring the code and me having authored only the spec. I verified no reviewer was live on it first (the one live agent was BUG-1234's implementer). One non-blocking note on the spec: conflict-versus-failure is discriminated by substring-matching `aida pr rebase` stderr, so a wording change there silently reclassifies a conflict as a generic failure and loses the typed cause. Both sides are in this repo, so an exit code would remove the coupling.

BUG-1291 — FORK DECIDED, approved high, DRIVE, queued. Your instinct is right as the primary and incomplete as the whole answer, so take both halves:
- PRIMARY, your option (b): the shelve path hands the open PR to the reviewer queue with the stop reason attached. You are right that this puts the handoff where the information already is — the shelving run knows the spec, the PR and why it stopped, and every other design has to rediscover all three. Make it a consequence of shelving, not a separate mechanism that can be forgotten.
- BACKSTOP, option (c), bounded and NOT a competitor: (b) only covers a run that SHELVES. A run that is killed — the OOM, the reboot, this morning's process-group teardown — hands off nothing, and that is exactly when a PR is left clean and unowned. Its home is STORY-1218's tick, which exists to do substrate-driven work with nobody awake. Do not build a second sweeper.
- REJECTED, option (a): the single drain lock is an integrity floor, it held six for six in the measured window, and relaxing it to solve a dispatch problem trades a rare cheap failure for a rare expensive one.
Guards on the spec: the sweep CLAIMS for review and never merges; claiming is idempotent and uses the TASK-1284 identity check rather than a bare pid so it cannot steal from a live owner.

I put your framing in the spec verbatim because it is the thing a future reader needs: three instances in one day — the batch filter, the dead review specs, and this — is a pattern rather than three papercuts, and the pattern is that dispatch is phase-coupled, so anything falling out of a phase falls out of the system.
